name: libRSVG
baseline: resvg 0.8.0 (cairo, Qt, raqote and Skia backends) and QtSvg 5.12.3
workload: Wall time to render every SVG file of two icon themes (Oxygen 4.12, 4947 files with heavy blur, clipping and masking; Elementary OS 5.0, 3417 simple files) with librsvg 2.45.5 versus resvg 0.8.0 backends and QtSvg 5.12.3.
claimed_speedup: Oxygen 4.12: librsvg 2.45.5 163 s versus resvg 0.8.0 cairo 195 s, qt 191 s, raqote 205 s, skia 175 s (about 1.2x faster than resvg-cairo, derived from page data); QtSvg 5.12.3 160 s. Elementary 5.0: librsvg 24 s versus resvg qt 35 s and QtSvg 30 s, but resvg cairo, raqote and skia need only 19 s (librsvg is slower there).
stars_or_usage: GNOME's SVG renderer; 410 stars on the read-only GitHub mirror
tradeoffs: LGPL-2.1-or-later (Rust core with a C ABI, renders to Cairo surfaces). The resvg author attributes the Oxygen win to a faster blur implementation and native cairo clipping, which he says is incorrect for some inputs (resvg-test-suite clipPath row) but faster; librsvg therefore trades some SVG correctness for speed in that comparison.
caveats: Numbers are bar-chart labels in two SVG images (perf-oxygen.svg, perf-elementary.svg) in the resvg 0.8.0 repository, measured by the resvg author (a competitor, independent of librsvg); the benchmark README of that tag says all tested applications have different SVG support, which impacts the performance, and that Inkscape, Chrome, Firefox and Batik were left out for startup time. v0.8.0 states no CPU, compiler flags or librsvg build configuration and links no script (the v0.9.0 and v0.9.1 READMEs name an AMD 3700X, single thread, tmpfs, script in resvg-test-suite/tools/perf, but those charts dropped librsvg), so the tier is capped at C. librsvg 2.45.5 dates from 2019; librsvg has changed a lot since (no recent third-party rerun reached). librsvg loses to resvg on the simple Elementary set (24 s versus 19 s) and QtSvg is as fast on Oxygen (160 s) only because it skips filters, clipPath, mask and pattern. A WebSearch snippet (page not opened, blocked) mentions a later table with rsvg 2.42.2 at 242 s versus Inkscape 0.92.4 at 1610 s and Batik 1.12 at 3686 s on the W3C suite; not used in the record. The GNOME wiki, gitlab.gnome.org and librsvg's own benchmark tool were blocked; the repo_url is the GitHub mirror (canonical home is gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/librsvg). Same chart README: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RazrFalcon/resvg/v0.8.0/README.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RazrFalcon/resvg/v0.8.0/.github/perf-elementary.svg

name: libsixel
workload: 100 sequential runs of the img2sixel command line (libsixel 1.10.5) encoding one 256x256 JPEG (Lenna) to Sixel, output to /dev/null, versus the same for chafa and sixrs.
claimed_speedup: img2sixel 1.10.5 1.64 s for 100 runs versus chafa 1.18.2 7.32 s (about 4.5x faster, derived from page data); sixrs 1.66 s (a tie with img2sixel). Output sizes: img2sixel 121,993 bytes, chafa 4,248,878 bytes, sixrs 59,220 bytes.
compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.93.1 for sixrs only; libsixel and chafa builds and flags not stated; commands: img2sixel -p 256 -w 256 -h 256 -E fast -S, chafa -f sixels --size 256x256 -c 256 --animate off
stars_or_usage: 2.9k stars; Sixel library behind img2sixel and used by many terminal tools
tradeoffs: C library with an autotools build and bindings for Python, Perl, PHP and Ruby; the main license is MIT with seven further licences for bundled components (stb_image and others), all permissive. Several image loaders and a long CVE fix list in 1.8.7 (use-after-free and integer overflows in GIF, PNG and encoder paths) mean untrusted inputs need care.
caveats: The only numbers found are in the README of the sixrs crate (a competing Rust Sixel encoder, crate created 2026-06-29, 102 downloads, no repository link on crates.io), described there as a quick smoke benchmark and 'workload-specific'. Each run is a separate process on a 256x256 image, so startup cost dominates; chafa writes a 35x larger output (different dithering, palette and compression), so the tools do different work; img2sixel was run with -E fast and -S (fast encode, no sixel size optimisation) while chafa ran with its defaults. CPU model, libsixel and chafa build flags and the repo for the harness are not given, so this stays tier C. libsixel's own README, NEWS, ChangeLog and docs carry no benchmark numbers; the project emphasises quality and compatibility. libsixel's own site and the man pages were not opened.
